newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE PUTTS HIS WAY TO GRAND PRIX TITLE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE PUTTS HIS WAY TO GRAND PRIX TITLE.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie equalled the course record to win the European Grand Prix by five strokes on Sunday.
Montgomerie's 30 strokes on the final nine holes included four birdies over the closing five holes, to take him to 18-under-par 270 as he closed with a seven-under-par 65.

The 33-year-old Scot recorded his 13th victory in 10 years on the European Tour, going two better than his winning prediction before the event to leave defending champion Retief Goosen trailing in second place.
Montgomerie sealed his first victory of the year with some superb finishing, holing putts of 25ft, 35ft, 25ft and 12ft at the last.
His timely form, with only two bogeys in 93 holes of golf, put him in a buoyant mood ahead of this week's U.S. Open.
"I've been 26-under-par for my last five rounds of golf and made only two bogeys," he said.
"In the US Open it's not so much a case of the birdies you make but the bogeys you don't make and I can't wait for this coming Thursday morning the way things are going."
Goosen trailed Montgomerie by a stroke early in the round but his challenge was blown away by Montgomerie's finish and the South African had to settle for second place after hitting a 69.

England's Lee Westwood, who started the final round with Goosen just one shot behind Montgomerie, was third after hitting a 70 for a total of 276 and moved into seventh place in the Ryder Cup rankings.

Montgomerie moved to top of the European points table and climbed to fifth in the order of merit, but still trailed current leader Ian Woosnam of Wales by 168,035 points in his bid for a record fifth European rankings title.
